department everybody hear me all right okay as you know a couple of years ago we spun up our directed patrol unit members of council most of the members of council here had an opportunity to have a demonstration of the that directed patrol unit performed for you here that explained their roles within the community but for those of you that that do not know what it is or haven't had that opportunity I'll give a really brief explanation it's a group or unit of five officers three canine officers and two patrol officers that specifically target quality of life issues in the city of Lancaster so for instance your typical patrol officer that you see on the street you can give them neighborhood concerns you can give them issues going on in your community and they will work them and they'll do their due diligence and working them but if they get distracted or call away to another call for service or back up somewhere else in the city they can't concentrate all their time on that on that quality of life issue so the director patrol unit compiles all that information to a database and works that and specifically targets those issues and some members of council have actually utilized that unit for their constituents when they've had issues in their area and they're very highly effective the reason that I another portion of what they do unfortunately the nationwide drug epidemic forces them to conduct a portion of their role for narcotics enforcement a significant portion and the reason I highlight that is it'd be easy for me to stand up here and have political speak and say hey if you invest in the police department you'll have a better work product you'll have faster response times whatever it is but i think probably what the citizens are looking for and what you're looking for is a real world example on the streets of of the effectiveness of this unit and i i have that tonight that i would like to highlight um so a short time ago officer evanichko with the director patrol unit as canine barry had a traffic stop in the city of lancaster and as a result of that traffic stop they developed information that identified and led to one of the main suppliers of drugs and weapons in the city of Lancaster. The rest of the directed patrol unit piled on that information and over the course the next several weeks worked that information and conducted additional traffic stops, obtained additional statements, conducted other interviews, and obtained evidence as a result of that information and worked that to further concrete the probable cause on that individual. They relayed that relayed that information to the major crimes unit who's our investigative arm for narcotics enforcement locally and together they worked that information to develop probable cause on this individual and we brought in our federal partners at the ATF to assist with this. Major crimes unit picked up right where we left off. This investigation was worked and just last week it came to the culmination of what you see in front of you. The execution of this search warrant late last week resulted in the seizure of 18 firearms, 18 handguns, nine and a half pounds of methamphetamine, 3.17 pounds of fentanyl, 2.8 pounds of cocaine, along with hundreds of grams of heroin and Xanax. To put that in perspective, two milligrams of fentanyl can kill any one of us in this room. So to take 3.17 pounds off the street means that over 700,000 lethal doses of fentanyl in those firearms, methamphetamine, heroin, cocaine, are all off the streets of Lancaster, Ohio, because of the work that these individuals did. I am infinitely proud of Officer Evanichko and K-9 Barry, Officer Pierce and K-9 Omega, Officer Malone and K-9 Mechie, Officer Rennie and Officer Delgado, and the work that all the men and women at the Lancaster Police Department do every single day. I don't think people get an accurate picture of the work and the danger these officers deal with and the things they take off the street of this city, and i am honored to work beside them and these guys deserve all the credit thank you thank you
